title: Cleft Sentences
subtitle: Rearrange a sentence to put the most important information front and center.
objectives: Form "It is/was...that" clefts to emphasize a specific part of a sentence
Form "What...is/was" clefts to emphasize an action or idea

content.intro: A cleft sentence splits one idea into two clauses, putting the most important piece of information first, for emphasis — very common in both spoken and written English.

rules.heading: a) It is/was...that
rules.body:
Used to emphasize a specific person, thing, time or place.

  • John broke the window. → It was John who broke the window. (emphasizing WHO)
  • I met her at the conference. → It was at the conference that I met her. (emphasizing WHERE)

rules.heading: b) What...is/was
rules.body:
Used to emphasize an action, thing, or idea — often what someone wants, needs, likes, or did.

  • I need more time. → What I need is more time.
  • She annoyed me by being late. → What annoyed me was her being late.

examples: It was John who broke the window.
It was at the conference that I met her.
What I need is more time.
What annoyed me was her being late.
It's the price that worries me, not the quality.
What surprised everyone was his sudden resignation.

commonMistakes.wrong: It was John which broke the window.
commonMistakes.right: It was John who broke the window.
commonMistakes.why: For a person, use "who," not "which," after the cleft "It was..."

commonMistakes.wrong: What I need it's more time.
commonMistakes.right: What I need is more time.
commonMistakes.why: Only one verb "is/was" is needed to link the two clauses — don't add "it's" as well.

commonMistakes.wrong: Is the price that worries me.
commonMistakes.right: It's the price that worries me.
commonMistakes.why: The cleft needs "it" as the subject at the start — don't drop it.

items.prompt: ___ was John who broke the window.

items.explanation: "What...is" links the emphasized idea to the rest of the sentence.

items.prompt: It was at the conference ___ I met her.
What surprised everyone ___ his sudden resignation.
items.explanation: Past tense linking verb, matching the rest of the sentence.

items.prompt: Which cleft correctly emphasizes "the price," not the quality?
options: It's the price that worries me.
The price it's that worries me.

items.prompt: "She annoyed me by being late." — which cleft version is correct?
options: What annoyed me was her being late.
It was her being late what annoyed me.
What was annoyed me her being late.
items.explanation: "What...was" correctly emphasizes the cause of the annoyance.

items.incorrect: It was Maria which called you.
answer: It was Maria who called you.

items.incorrect: What I want it's a quiet weekend.
answer: What I want is a quiet weekend.
items.explanation: Only one linking verb is needed — remove the extra "it's."

summary: It is/was...that/who = emphasize a specific person, thing, time or place.
What...is/was = emphasize an action, need, or idea.
Only one linking verb (is/was) connects the two halves — don't double it up.
